/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 08 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3584 (9)
Baltic Capesize Index: 6313 (27)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2414 (-17)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1693 (11)
Baltic Handysize Index: 913 (7)
CAPESIZE
The market maintained its positive momentum today, with the BCI 182 5TC gaining a further $242 to $57,253. In the Pacific, the C5 index rose by 0.310 to $18.520 following a busy day of activity yesterday, with sentiment slightly firmer and owners continuing to hold their ground. After yesterday's flurry of business in the low $18s, offers opened in the upper $18s. One miner improved its bid to $18.00 and was heard trading around $18.50 before concluding at $18.40. A second miner was said to be seeing offers at $18.70 before reportedly fixing at $18.50. With operators noticeably quiet, brokers expect a premium to be paid for suitable tonnage, particularly as the market remains well supported. The Atlantic also saw a modest uptick in activity, with C3 becoming increasingly positional. Bids were heard from the low to mid $41s, with $41.80 bid against offers around $42.50 and as high as $43.00 depending on specific dates. The C3 index itself was little changed, edging up just 0.132 to $41.682.
PANAMAX
Sentiment in the Atlantic remained mostly negative, a view widely shared among market participants, who continued to highlight a persistent imbalance between supply and demand. An oversupply of prompt tonnage, particularly in the North Continent, continued to weigh on the market amid a distinct lack of demand. Brokers noted that, while sentiment has softened, owners have so far resisted drastically revising their trans-Atlantic offers significantly lower. By comparison, fronthaul business was said to be relatively more stable, supported by steadier demand from both the coal and grain trades although the P2A posted a move downwards. Market sources described it as a relatively quiet day in the Pacific, with demand for spot tonnage able to make Indonesia and Australia easing. The slowdown in enquiry levels is said to have resulted in a more subdued trading environment, with charterers showing less urgency in covering requirements. The Golden Ginger (81,507 2012) open in Kunsan 13 September was discussed as being placed on subjects for a North Pacific trip to Singapore-Japan range around $22,500 to Pan Ocean. The Minoan Ocean (93,146 2011) open Vung Ang 11 September was said to have been fixed, although no other details surfaced. The P5TC fell by a further $154 to conclude at $21,724.
SUPRAMAX
Limited reported trades after such a quiet day yesterday, but a positive Index today with the 11TC average up $136 to $21,403. The North American market again saw the biggest improvement, but the Mediterranean also turned the corner and returned a decent increase having been under pressure for a while. Sentiment in the East remains strong with rates continuing to show small gains, and the Indian Ocean also looks well supported. The Xin Hai Tong 52 (56,799 2011) prompt Nantong was fixed for a trip via Gulf of Aden to the Mediterranean at $23,000, the Dubai Nature (64,001 2025) Fujairah prompt fixed a trip via Duqm to East Africa intention DAP in bulk at around $18,000 with XO (scrubber for Charterers benefit) and the Merchia (63,800 2015) was said to be on subjects basis delivery Richards Bay Coal Terminal for a trip either to Sri Lanka at $25,500 plus $255,000 ballast bonus, or to East coast India at $26,000 plus $260,000 ballast bonus with Oldendorff.
HANDYSIZE
Another quiet day was seen in the Handy sector, with sentiment remaining generally firm across both the Atlantic and Pacific basins. The BHSI closed at 913, while the 7TC average gained $122 to end the day at $16,425. In the Continent and Mediterranean, only minor movements were reported, and the market remained balanced, with rates marginally firmer than previous levels. The US Gulf and South Atlantic continued to show upward momentum, despite limited fixture activity materialising so far. Market participants remained cautiously optimistic, as rates continued to show signs of strengthening. A 49,000-dwt vessel open West Africa was heard fixed for a trip via Owendo to China with manganese ore at around $18,500–$19,000, although further details were not disclosed. The Asian market also experienced another quiet session, with the tonnage list appearing relatively shorter while enquiries continued to be discussed at healthy levels. A 40,000-dwt newbuilding from Japan was fixed to the Continent via COGH at $20,000, although further details were not disclosed.
